claims.claim: V4-Pro 1.6T total / 49B activated, 33T tokens; V4-Flash 284B / 13B, 32T tokens; 1M context
At 1M context: Pro 27% single-token FLOPs and 10% KV cache of V3.2; Flash 10% and 7%; FLOPs in FP8-equivalent; Figure 1 annotations 3.7x/9.8x lower FLOPs, 9.5x/13.7x smaller KV
CSA compresses every m tokens into one entry from 2m overlapping entries with learned positional bias; lightning indexer selects top-k; shared-KV MQA; grouped output projection
HCA compresses every m'=128 tokens without overlap, dense attention over all compressed entries
RMSNorm on query heads and compressed KV; partial RoPE on last 64 dims with RoPE(-i) on outputs; 128-token sliding-window branch; learnable sink in softmax denominator
BF16 for RoPE dims, FP8 for the rest; indexer attention in FP4; smaller top-k than V3.2; KV about 2% of BF16 GQA8 head-dim-128 baseline at 1M

Flash 43 layers, d=4096, first two layers pure SWA, CSA m=4 top-k 512, HCA m'=128, 64 query heads, head dim 512, 1 shared + 256 routed experts top-6, hash routing first 3 MoE layers, MTP depth 1, mHC n=4 t_max=20; Pro 61 layers, d=7168, first two layers HCA, top-k 1024, 128 heads, 384 routed experts top-6
Affinity Sigmoid -> Sqrt(Softplus); auxiliary-loss-free balancing plus sequence-wise loss 0.0001; node-limit removed; dense FFN in first blocks replaced with hash-routed MoE; MTP unchanged from V3
Muon for most matrices; AdamW for embedding, head, mHC static biases and gates, RMSNorm; hybrid Newton-Schulz 8+2 steps; no QK-Clip because Q/KV RMSNorm
4K -> 16K -> 64K -> 1M; Flash dense attention for first 1T tokens, sparse introduced at 64K after indexer warmup; Pro has a longer dense stage (length not given)

Notable loss spikes tied to MoE outliers; Anticipatory Routing (~20% wall-clock overhead when active, triggered only on spikes) and SwiGLU clamping (linear [-10,10], gate upper bound 10); mechanism not understood
State cache for SWA and uncompressed tail; blocks of lcm(m,m') tokens; on-disk compressed KV; SWA KV ~8x compressed KV; full / periodic / zero SWA caching, zero requires recomputing n_win x L tokens
LongBench-V2 V3.2-Base 40.2, V4-Flash-Base 44.7, V4-Pro-Base 51.5; Flash-Base below V3.2-Base on BigCodeBench 56.8 vs 63.9 and MATH 57.4 vs 60.5
MRCR 1M: Opus-4.6 92.9, Gemini-3.1-Pro 76.3, V4-Pro-Max 83.5; CorpusQA 1M: 71.7, 53.8, 62.0; Flash Non-think MRCR 37.5 vs Max 78.7, CorpusQA 15.5 vs 60.5
MRCR 8-needle average MMR, Pro-Max: 0.90/0.85/0.94/0.90/0.92 for 8K–128K, 0.82 at 256K, 0.66 at 512K, 0.59 at 1M; Flash-Max 0.49 at 1M

Opus 4.5 52.0% vs 45.9% on hardest writing prompts; white-collar weaknesses (format constraints, concise summaries, slide aesthetics); coding survey N=85 notes trivial mistakes, vague-prompt misreading, over-thinking
EP fused kernel 1.50–1.73x, up to 1.96x; mHC overhead 6.7% of 1F1B stage; BF16 index scores 2x top-k speedup with 99.7% recall

Architecture relatively complex because many preliminarily validated components retained; stability tricks not understood; future: sparser embedding modules (Engram), low-latency architectures, multimodal

Reconstructed global KV bytes/token: V2 69,120 (BF16, 60 layers); V3.2 61 x (656+132) = 48,068; V4-Flash 21 x (584+68)/4 + 20 x 584/128 = 3,514; V4-Pro 30 x 163 + 31 x 4.5625 ~= 5,031; matches V4.1 Figure 1(b) and V4 Figure 1 ratio 9.5x
